tasks.spec:
You are a code worker. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of freytag-forge; edit files here directly. Do NOT git commit. You own ONLY: storygame/runtime/reference_resolution.py (new), storygame/runtime/engine.py, tests/test_reference_resolution.py (new), tests/test_reference_clarification.py (new). Touch nothing else (not web_demo.py, not the frontend, not data/, not cloudflare.py, not recent_cue.py). Never weaken or delete an existing test; if an existing test outside your files fails because of your change, stop and report which one and why.

GOAL (Stage 4 items 2-4 of .plans/implementation_plan.md, engine core only). Build scene-local bare-noun resolution and a fixed clarification question inside the engine, story-neutral (no story ids or story words in runtime code). A short noun the player types ("terminal") should mean the thing placed in the scene the player is in; when two or more things there share that head noun, the engine asks a fixed system question instead of narrating, Inform-style. Design history: the 2026-10-06 design in git history (`git show 5ea0119955c62b84699a8dc7878a4af770b55a7e:.plans/scene-affordance-e2e.md`, section 'Plan item: resolve a bare noun against the player's current scene') and its offline simulation scripts/ringer/affordance/bare_name_sim.py. Read both. Changes from that design, decided by Brandon on 2026-10-16: the pending question is NOT stored anywhere on the server. It is CLIENT-HELD: the caller passes the original command back in as `clarifies` together with a `clarification_round`; the engine re-derives the ambiguity from the current state. No RuntimeState field, no snapshot change, no map, nothing persisted. Rule 'a question never survives a reload' therefore holds by construction.

CONTRACT.
New module storygame/runtime/reference_resolution.py:
  @dataclass(frozen=True) class Clarification: original_command: str; noun: str; options: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]  # (entity_id, display name), deterministic order; round: int
  @dataclass(frozen=True) class ReferenceResult: command: str; question: Clarification | None; outcome: str  # 'passthrough' | 'resolved' | 'asked' | 'answered' | 'dropped' | 'capped'; original: str; resolutions: tuple[tuple[str,str], ...]  # (noun, entity_id)
  def resolve_references(state, player_input, *, clarifies: str | None = None, clarification_round: int = 0) -> ReferenceResult
  def clarification_text(clarification) -> str  # fixed line, e.g. 'Do you mean the archive terminals or the medical terminal?' (three or more: 'a, b, or c'). Use 'the' + lowercase name for lowercase names and the bare name for proper names, reusing the article helpers in storygame/runtime/fixed_refusal.py/taking.py rather than duplicating them.
engine.py: RuntimeEngine.turn(self, player_input, *, clock_seconds=None, clarifies=None, clarification_round=0) stays backward compatible (new kwargs default None/0). New class ClarificationTurn shaped like the existing EngineRefusalTurn (segments with one narration segment holding clarification_text, selected_knowledge_ids=(), events=(), game_break=None, story_complete=False, narration property) plus a `.clarification` attribute (the Clarification). The engine stores the latest ReferenceResult on `self.last_reference_resolution` (None when no resolution ran) for telemetry.

SEMANTICS (all required).
1. Where it runs: at the top of RuntimeEngine.turn BEFORE `_begin_provider_turn`, the provider, the projector, capture and any state change. If the story is complete or a game break is pending, skip resolution entirely (passthrough). Resolution only reads state.
2. Scope = things currently in the player's scene according to the live facts/world model, not static scene metadata: reuse the existing runtime notion of 'in the protagonist's scene' (see storygame/runtime/knowledge.py::_entity_in_scene_scope and scoped_alias_entity_ids, KnowledgeProjector's in_scene set, world_model.world_for, and how storygame/runtime/capture.py/fixed_refusal.py compute in_scope). Pick ONE existing definition, say which in a docstring, and do not invent a second one. Consider items, npcs and groups (not locations, not the protagonist).
3. Matching: a 'bare head noun' is the LAST word of an in-scope thing's name or of one of its scoped_aliases (not plain aliases), lowercased, longer than 2 characters, not a stopword (the, a, of, to, my, her, his, and the like). A word is NOT bare if the command already names a thing in full: strip every full name/alias form of every entity (any scene) from the command text first, exactly as bare_name_sim.py does with `rest`, and only look for bare words in what remains (full-name precedence). Match whole words, with simple singular/plural tolerance only if bare_name_sim.py did not need it (do not add fuzzy matching).
4. Outcomes per bare noun: exactly one in-scope thing has that head -> resolved silently: the command handed onward has that bare word replaced by the thing's full name (case-insensitive whole word, once); none -> untouched. Two or more distinct things share the head -> ambiguous. If ANY noun in the command is ambiguous the engine asks about the first ambiguous noun (stable order: position in the command) and returns ClarificationTurn without running the turn: provider NOT called, turn_index unchanged, no facts, no TurnRecord, no cue/pacing/clock change, no attempt record. Resolution of other unambiguous nouns is not applied on an asking turn (the original command travels in the clarification).
5. Answers: when `clarifies` is given, first re-derive the question for `clarifies` in the CURRENT scene. If it is no longer ambiguous (e.g. the scene changed) -> outcome 'dropped': treat player_input as a fresh command (round 0). If it is ambiguous, try player_input as an answer: (a) it contains one option's full name; (b) it contains a word that appears in exactly one option's name and not in the others' (a distinguishing word such as 'medical'; 'the medical one'); (c) an ordinal 'first'/'second'/'third' (or '1st','2nd'...) selecting that option by its listed order. On a match splice the chosen option's full name over the ambiguous noun in `clarifies`, run resolution on the spliced command at clarification_round+1 and proceed ('answered'); if the spliced command still has ANOTHER ambiguous noun and the round counter is below the cap, ask again with round+1; the cap is TWO question rounds in total: when clarification_round+1 >= 2 and anything is still ambiguous, do not ask again, run the spliced command with remaining ambiguous nouns left untouched ('capped'). If player_input matches no option (unrelated input) -> outcome 'dropped': the question is cancelled and player_input runs as a fresh command (it may itself ask a NEW question at round 0).
6. No reveal is granted solely by resolution: resolution only rewrites command text; reveal evidence, eligibility, prerequisites and validation are untouched. The rewritten command is what `_turn_active` receives as player_input; `self.last_reference_resolution.original` keeps the player's words.
7. Do not touch the narrator prompt text, guides, package data, or the recent-cue projection (storygame/runtime/recent_cue.py runs later inside the provider and must keep working: its tests must still pass).

TESTS (hermetic, offline, no network; ruff-clean, line length 120; follow the style of tests/test_1a_gap_pointer.py and tests/test_recent_cue_unit.py). Use the real continuity-initiative package (Path('data/stories/continuity-initiative')) and bench.core.advance_state_to_scene(PACKAGE, state, '2B') etc. First find, with a throwaway script (not committed), which in-scope head-word collisions really exist in each scene using the real world (bare_name_sim.py's census found 'terminal' in 2B: archive terminals vs medical terminal; 'seat' in 1A; 'corridors'/'level' in 2C) and use those real cases; build synthetic packages only where the real story has no case (copy the package object in memory; never edit data/).
tests/test_reference_resolution.py (pure function): unique in-scope head resolves to the full name; two things ask with the exact fixed text and deterministic option order; full-name precedence ('Read the messages on the medical terminal.' asks nothing); scoped alias head counts; a head word of a thing NOT in scope passes through unchanged (wrong-target negative); plain alias head words do NOT count; collision of an unrelated bare word leaves the command alone; answer by full name, by distinguishing word, by ordinal; unrelated input drops the question and returns outcome 'dropped' with the input unchanged; a changed scene drops it; round cap (a command with two ambiguous nouns, answer the first, the second is asked at most once more, a third never); resolution never mutates state (deepcopy compare model_dump excluding package before/after).
tests/test_reference_clarification.py (engine level, using a provider callable that counts calls and returns a minimal valid reply, like tests/test_recent_cue_reference.py / tests/test_1a_gap_pointer.py helpers): an asking turn returns ClarificationTurn, provider call count 0, state.turn_index/facts/turn_records/delivered_cue_ids unchanged, `.clarification` populated, narration equals the fixed line; the answering turn runs normally with the spliced command (provider receives the spliced command, turn_index +1); an unrelated reply runs as a fresh command; scene-change drop; save/load round trip of state mid-question has nothing to restore because nothing was stored (assert `'clarif' not in state.model_dump_json()` style: no new field on RuntimeState); a resolved unique head reaches the provider rewritten; story_complete and pending-break states pass through untouched; engine.turn without the new kwargs behaves exactly as before; no reveal is granted by resolution alone (a command whose only change is the resolved name but whose action evidence is unmet earns nothing).

HOW TO RUN. First confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside this worktree. Then, for fast iteration, `PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q --no-cov -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_reference_resolution.py tests/test_reference_clarification.py tests/test_recent_cue_reference.py tests/test_recent_cue_unit.py`; before finishing run the whole suite once with `-n 4` (about 2 minutes) and ruff check / ruff format --check on your four files via /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/ruff.

COMPLETION RULE: do not stop until the module, the engine hook, both test files and the full suite pass with ruff clean. In your final message list the files changed, which scope definition you reused, the real collisions you found per scene, and paste the pytest summary line.
tasks.verified: scene-local bare-noun resolution and a client-held fixed clarification question work in the engine without narration, facts, clock or stored state
